pr_title: PipeWire: stop log spam from RequestProcess events
pr_body:
## Description
<!--- Provide a general summary of your change in the Pull Request title above -->
<!--- Describe your change in detail here. -->

This PR fixes an issue where PipeWire error logs are continuously created whenever there is audio playing or if the "keep audio device alive" setting is enabled.

This issue has appeared ever since PipeWire [v1.2.4](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/compare/1.2.3...1.2.4) introduced a [change](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/commit/c6ae68b9326f235aa6ee11b62b8e6a9126bb2e22) that forwards RequestProcess events.

These events are emitted whenever [`pw_stream_trigger_process()`](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/b794e3660961ad23246035ddd78eabd607581615/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Sinks/pipewire/PipewireStream.cpp#L78) is called, which then tries to send RequestProcess commands (`command 10`) to a driver that fails with the error.

Since the stream is a driver, as set by [`PW_STREAM_FLAG_DRIVER`](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/b794e3660961ad23246035ddd78eabd607581615/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Sinks/pipewire/AESinkPipewire.cpp#L463), we should only call `pw_stream_trigger_process()` when the stream is driving by checking [`pw_stream_is_driving()`](https://docs.pipewire.org/group__pw__stream.html#ga3ddd332c45aa95250d3d1d26cf01452a). This allows [`do_trigger_driver()`](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/e4ff13a75d7acf170f6094db148dc77f380d505a/src/pipewire/stream.c#L2598) to be called while not allowing RequestProcess events to be emitted when the stream is not driving.

The [`(impl->trigger)` condition](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/e4ff13a75d7acf170f6094db148dc77f380d505a/src/pipewire/stream.c#L2594) only applies when the stream has `PW_STREAM_FLAG_TRIGGER` set, which is not the case [here](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/b794e3660961ad23246035ddd78eabd607581615/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Sinks/pipewire/AESinkPipewire.cpp#L461).

## Motivation and context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->

This PR fixes #26122.

Other users have also reported the same [issue](https://forum.endeavouros.com/t/thousands-of-pipewire-errors/61069/8).

## How has this been tested?
<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your change. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->

I have tested this fix to be working on Arch (PipeWire v1.2.7) and Ubuntu 24.10 (PipeWire v1.2.4).

## What is the effect on users?
<!--- Summarize the effect of this change on Kodi end-users. -->
<!--- If the PR does not have a noticeable impact (e.g., if it only changes documentation), -->
<!--- just leave it empty. Put in more detail the bigger the impact is. -->
<!--- This section may be used for automatic creation of release notes. -->

This change will stop logging errors continuously whenever there is audio playback.

issue_context.title: Omega spams pipewire 1.2.4 logs with 2x10 "spa.audioadapter: 0x55679102b8: can't send command 10: Operation not supported" per second
issue_context.body:
<!--- Please fill out this template to the best of your ability. You can always edit this issue once you have created it. -->
<!--- Read the following link before you create a new problem report: https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Submit_a_bug_report  -->

## Bug report
### Describe the bug
Here is a clear and concise description of what the problem is:
<!--- Provide a more detailed introduction to the issue itself, and why you consider it to be a bug -->
<!--- A bug report that is not clear will be closed -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
**AudioEngine calls pw_stream_trigger_process in an incompatible way**

When using Kodi21 below RaspberryPi-OS to play Audio from GUI sounds or DVB-T2 it keeps spamming the pipewire processes logs with messages like:
`pipewire[767] spa.audioadapter: 0x55679102b8: can't send command 10: Operation not supported`
The log entry seems to occur 20 times per second.


## Expected Behavior
Here is a clear and concise description of what was expected to happen:
<!--- Tell us what should happen -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->

Kodi uses Pipewire in a way that doesn't lead to log spam.


## Actual Behavior
<!--- Tell us what happens instead -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
while audio just seems to play just fine it looks like

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/Omega/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Sinks/pipewire/PipewireStream.cpp#L78 seems to call
the method `pw_stream_trigger_process`
from https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/1.2.4/src/pipewire/stream.c#L2537

https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/1.2.4/spa/plugins/audioconvert/audioadapter.c#L987 shows that the invalid [command 10](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/8f7acb717cda83f78fc128112e30d9b68337b2bd/spa/include/spa/node/type-info.h#L47) maybe unsupported by either the triggerer device would cause the same log message to be produced.

## Possible Fix
<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix or reason for the bug -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
Pipewire seems to have two modes of using streams, (self)"driving" or by being triggered.

Kodi should use this method (existing since pw 0.3.4 and thus [allowed](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/Omega/CMakeLists.txt#L243) by kodi) `pw_stream_is_driving` to check weather the stream is "driving" and should be triggered explicitly.
https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/1.2.4/src/pipewire/stream.h#L566

It could still be that this is just a bug in pw, since I could have messed up my understanding of driving and triggered pw usage.


### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
<!--- Provide a link to a live example, or an unambiguous set of steps to -->
<!--- reproduce this bug. Include code to reproduce, if relevant -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
1. install kodi21 on a recent raspberryPi OS with pipewire 1.2.4
2. play audio e.g. by navigating menues or watching a video
3. watch `journalctl -b -0 -f` for some seconds


### Debuglog
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
<!--- A debuglog is always mandatory when creating an issue. Provide one! -->
The debuglog can be found here:
debug log https://paste.kodi.tv/ciqaveyuca.kodi
journalctl pw debug log https://paste.kodi.tv/feniwijade created with `PIPEWIRE_DEBUG=E,spa.audioadapter:D`

## Additional context or screenshots (if appropriate)
Here is some additional context or explanation that might help:
<!--- How has this bug affected you? What were you trying to accomplish? -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->

### Screenshots
Here are some links or screenshots to help explain the problem:
<!--- Put your text below this line -->

### Your Environment
Used Operating system:
<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->
<!--- Put your text below this line. Checkboxes can easily be ticked once issue is created -->
 - [ ] Android
 - [ ] iOS
 - [ ] tvOS
 - [x] Linux
 - [ ] macOS
 - [ ] Windows
 - [ ] Windows UWP

 - Operating system version/name:
/etc/rpi-issue 
Raspberry Pi reference 2024-11-19
Generated using pi-gen, https://github.com/RPi-Distro/pi-gen, 891df1e21ed2b6099a2e6a13e26c91dea44b34d4, stage4
/etc/debian_version
12.8
 - Kodi version:
   Kodi Media Center 21.1 (21.1.0) Git:20241025-f41df4d7da / package 3:21.1-5~bookworm

- pipewire 1.2.4-1~bpo12+1+rpt1


<!--- End of this issue -->

Team Kodi will consider your problem report however, we will not make any promises the problem will be solved.*
comments: i also see this behavior, on a full-fledged amd64 workstation. pipewire 1.2.7 on debian. kodi 21.1+dfsg-5+b1.

Sure - upstream issue, see the documentation:  https://docs.pipewire.org/group__pw__stream.html#gab93fa91d8ea80e562bb5e8f6b5bafe21 and file a bug upstream. Citation:

Streams that are **not** drivers according to [pw_stream_is_driving()](https://docs.pipewire.org/group__pw__stream.html#ga3ddd332c45aa95250d3d1d26cf01452a) can also call this method. The result is that a RequestProcess event is sent to the driver. If the graph is lazy scheduling according to [pw_stream_is_lazy()](https://docs.pipewire.org/group__pw__stream.html#gac987fb3ab601efd721dbd912e21b9136), this might result in a graph cycle by the driver. If the graph is not lazy scheduling **and the stream is not a driver, this method will have no effect.**

Don't we actually set the flag `PW_STREAM_FLAG_DRIVER` right here?
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/Omega/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Sinks/pipewire/AESinkPipewire.cpp#L463
https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/1.2.4/src/pipewire/stream.h#L566 states that in this case we should explicitly call `pw_stream_trigger_process` as we do.
But according to PW logs we can determine that this only leads to errors getting logged.
Since audio gets played despite those messages it looks like we are missing something :)
Also the description of stephans MR promises that using the check, both still plays audio AND silences the logs thus indicating the flag wasn't set for the stream after all.

I for my part were able to at least [silence the logs](https://docs.pipewire.org/page_daemon.html#:~:text=Logging) with
`.config/systemd/user/pipewire.service.d/debug.conf`:
```INI
[Service]
Environment="PIPEWIRE_DEBUG=W,pw.*:I,spa.audioadapter:X"
```

Yes - that's the case - you understand why I am hessitant to just merge it ... as we do totally fine according to documentation and even for setting the driver flag, right?

That one: https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/26125

review_comments:
Due to the design - the two commands are "non atomic". Means you could be scheduled away and condition when you call TriggerProcess might be the other way round already and your log comes back. As those two belong together, they need to be protected with a critical section.

Key question is: Is it worth it?

Also from the PW docu:
Streams that are not drivers according to [pw_stream_is_driving()](https://docs.pipewire.org/group__pw__stream.html#ga3ddd332c45aa95250d3d1d26cf01452a) can also call this method. The result is that a RequestProcess event is sent to the driver. If the graph is lazy scheduling according to [pw_stream_is_lazy()](https://docs.pipewire.org/group__pw__stream.html#gac987fb3ab601efd721dbd912e21b9136), this might result in a graph cycle by the driver. If the graph is not lazy scheduling and the stream is not a driver, this method will have no effect.

We are very well allowed to call it - even if we are not driving ...

Also - if you look how they use the tirgger in their example, most of the time in on_timeout / etc. I think - the official PW examples will spam the absolute same way, as they do not check for isDriving themselves.

I am not against that change -> but making an upstream bugreport - and asking for "best practice" would be good. PW is a very young technology for now and with every major release, some things change slightly, which is perfectly fine. From my POV though, we should not "workaround" things downstream where documentation states: "this method will have no effect".

Thanks for the review.

I initially did not think of using `pw_stream_is_driving()` with `pw_stream_trigger_process()` as I found removing `pw_stream_trigger_process()` altogether still allowed audio playback to work while not emitting RequestProcess events, but I assumed it must still be important for something.

I compiled my own PipeWire build to add some print statements to each conditional branch `pw_stream_trigger_process()` and found that `do_trigger_driver()` only gets called when "keep audio device alive" is disabled. Even then, it is only called occasionally when audio actually gets output. Most of the time any GUI action will not produce any sound. It seems to queue them up to play them all at once at a later point instead. This results in the logged error: `CActiveAESink::OutputSamples - failed`. This is unlike PulseAudio or ALSA, where GUI sounds always plays properly, whether "keep audio device alive" is on or off. However, that issue is resolved when `PW_STREAM_FLAG_DRIVER` is removed.

During times when the GUI is used but no sound plays, the `else` branch is executed in `pw_stream_trigger_process()`, emitting RequestProcess events. When sound is finally produced, we see that the `else if (stream->node->driving)` branch calls `do_trigger_driver()`. But even if `pw_stream_trigger_process()` never gets called, we still get proper sound. And as stated before, `(impl->trigger)` doesn't evaluate true without `PW_STREAM_FLAG_TRIGGER`. So it seems like `pw_stream_trigger_process()` isn't really doing anything, at least in my testing.

I compiled PipeWire's examples for video that include `pw_stream_trigger_process()` but was unable to run them so I can't confirm if it also spams the log. I was able to test out [`audio-src.c`](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/master/src/examples/audio-src.c), which plays an audio stream without any logs since it doesn't call `pw_stream_trigger_process()`.

Looking at the source for [pw-cat](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/master/src/tools/pw-cat.c) and other media players with PipeWire support ([mpv](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/blob/master/audio/out/ao_pipewire.c) and [MPD](https://github.com/MusicPlayerDaemon/MPD/blob/master/src/output/plugins/PipeWireOutputPlugin.cxx)), we can see that none of them use `pw_stream_trigger_process()` and playback doesn't log any errors. This led me to believe that the issue might be with Kodi instead of upstream but I can still open an upstream bug report if needed.

Additionally, if we use `wpctl` to inspect the stream nodes, we see that Kodi's `node.driver-id` is set to a sink node that is a driver (`node.driver = "true"`). So I'm not sure why we need to set Kodi's stream as a driver with `PW_STREAM_FLAG_DRIVER` when there is already a driver in the graph. The players mentioned also do not set their streams as a driver.

Maybe we can revisit #22442 and see if it would make sense to remove the changes that included `PW_STREAM_FLAG_DRIVER` and `pw_stream_trigger_process()`.

That is an interesting find. When keep audio alive packages are queued only, they would have no effect.

One reason why Kodi wants to be a driver is the delay management. We want to know and feel at all times that audio was consumed under the hood. Also by design audio engine in Kodi has a driving loop itself. The Kodi audio sink thread is only blocked by the PW sink implementation. So it is clear why driver design was chosen.

Need to check again where the bug is. The stream noise case rings my alarm bells in a sense of that stream trigger is anyways not fully working as we thought it works.

Thanks for looking into this!

It might be that PW does an idle detection and unloads us as a driver when AE stops adding samples when being in its idle state without being alive. That way you should only get it when pressing a button.

It might be that we have to reset the driving state. E.g. when it removed our driver state, we have to ask it again?  If (!driving) make it drive() followed by process?

There is no direct possibility (e.g. set_driving) available. There is the stream properties that could update it - but honestly - I think something is wrong here. Do you see that PW reports idle and unloads the sink?

With "keep audio device alive" disabled, a GUI action that doesn't produce sound when it should have will keep the Kodi stream node active (`wpctl status`) / running (`pw-top`). It will remain in this state even without audio playback or user interaction. Also, it will sometimes cause the error count in `pw-top` to increase continuously.

If we keep pressing a button until we finally get a GUI sound, `pw-top` shows the stream change to an idle state and the error count stops increasing. The stream node is removed shortly thereafter.

With "keep audio device alive" enabled, the Kodi stream node always remains in the running / active state, but each GUI sound will increase the error count by 4 or 5.

The description for errors from the `pw-top` man page:

> Xruns  for  drivers  are  when  the  graph did not complete a cycle. This can be because a node in the graph also has  an  Xrun.  It  can  also  be  caused  when scheduling delays cause a deadline to be missed, causing a hardware Xrun.
> 
> Xruns for followers are incremented when the node started processing but did not complete before the end of the graph cycle deadline.

Okay. That basically means, we properly have to issue timeouts in pipewire itself when the sink is not being used.

For the menu sounds: Yes, that is the reason we implemented keep audio alive in first place as HDMI receivers and others would simply shutdown.

I believe the lazy mechanism is more about screensharing, where frames might only be provided by the stream when something changes rather than on a clock.

This patch seems correct -- for audio, the expectation would be that the driver is generating process callbacks on its clock, and the rest of the graph nodes run their `process()` callback as a result -- so `pw_stream_trigger_process()` _must_ be called when the stream is driving, and _only_ when the stream is driving (there are some exceptions like in the loopback module where the playback stream opts out of process callbacks, and is triggered by the capture stream using the same API).

While I see why you might want to choose Kodi's clock as the driver, I assume that adapts to current delay? PipeWire will do rate matching on the ALSA node if it's following, but I can imagine this would get tricky with passthrough.

I could not track how the "keep device alive in idle" functionality works. There is a `PW_KEY_PAUSE_ON_IDLE` and `PW_KEY_SUSPEND_ON_IDLE`, but pause/suspend would only happen if your stream is unlinked or not providing data, so I would not expect that to happen if you're feeding in silence when nothing else is playing.

Hey @fritsch! Unfortunately, the [reconfiguration work](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pulseaudio/pulseaudio/-/merge_requests/24) we needed for HBR formats got caught up in a review cycle that didn't close before people lost interest / moved on to other things.

Most of the effort these days is on the PipeWire side anyway, so I'm not sure we'll ever complete that. The PulseAudio client libraries are still a fully supported (and in some cases recommended) API to talk to PipeWire, so maybe your branch + libpulse + pipewire-pulse will actually just work (and if not, I can take a look)

Thanks for the feedback. Actually I don't want to break kodi's long lasting pulsesink (Edit: by accident), but just keep it as is - pipewire seems to be the road forward, so therefore let's focus on that one.

Sure @fritsch, I have rebased it now.

Unfortunately, I don't have permission to add a backport label if that's what you meant. Please let me know if there is another way you would like me to mark it.

Thanks guys.
